review: Tactical chapter text and numeric cost/coverage rows inventoried. Facing, reach and multi-hex diagrams on B385/B388/B392 visually inspected; exact coordinate fixtures, vision diagram review and cross-rule precedence remain pending. Geometry and barrier assessments authored; coordinate fixtures unrun, complete path and figure-state coverage pending.

entries.acceptance: Each hex represents one yard. Human-sized or smaller combatants occupy one hex except actual close combat, swarms and noncombat crowding; up to four friendly ordinary humans can crowd without gaining normal fighting space.
entries.implementation_note: Owned single-hex encounter placement, finite map occupancy and receipts authored. Crowding, close combat, swarms, multi-hex footprints and movement integration remain pending; fixtures unrun.

entries.acceptance: A partly obstructed boundary hex counts as full unless the author rules otherwise. Fully solid hexes remain impassable; use explicit terrain facts, not center-point occupancy alone.
entries.implementation_note: Pure geometric/terrain assessment only. Owned positions, occupancy and path integration remain incomplete; fixtures unrun.

entries.acceptance: Store one of six headings; three adjacent directions are front, one left, one right and one back. Handedness determines weapon/shield sides. Rotation must preserve relative classification.
entries.implementation_note: Pure geometric/terrain assessment only. Owned positions, occupancy and path integration remain incomplete; fixtures unrun.

entries.acceptance: A human-sized prone or horizontal actor occupies two hexes. On falling, lower body remains in original hex and upper body occupies a selected legal neighbor; rising can use either occupied hex.

Committed attack moves before attacking, never afterward. It can stay, turn in place or move forward; movement permits two hexes or ceil(move/2) points, whichever is greater. It forbids end-of-move facing change. Reconcile the two-hex allowance with terrain costs explicitly.
Move and move-and-attack grant movement points equal to movement; increased dodge grants ceil(move/2). Other maneuver exceptions must not be replaced by one universal budget.
entries.implementation_note: Pure movement-value and heading assessments authored; persistent path execution, budget reconciliation and integration remain pending. Fixtures unrun.

entries.acceptance: Forward entry costs one point and goes into one of three front neighbors. Straight entry preserves facing; diagonal-front entry rotates one side toward the entered hex.
entries.implementation_note: Pure movement-value and heading assessments authored; persistent path execution, budget reconciliation and integration remain pending. Fixtures unrun.

entries.acceptance: Side/back movement preserves heading and costs two points, permitted for move, move-and-attack and increased dodge but not committed attack.
entries.implementation_note: Pure movement-value and heading assessments authored; persistent path execution, budget reconciliation and integration remain pending. Fixtures unrun.

entries.acceptance: A front-hex sidestep preserves heading at two points and is permitted during committed attack as well as other movement maneuvers.
entries.implementation_note: Pure movement-value and heading assessments authored; persistent path execution, budget reconciliation and integration remain pending. Fixtures unrun.

entries.acceptance: Rotating before/during eligible move, move-and-attack or increased dodge costs one point per hex-side. A half-turn costs three; do not confuse this with free final facing.
entries.implementation_note: Pure movement-value and heading assessments authored; persistent path execution, budget reconciliation and integration remain pending. Fixtures unrun.

entries.acceptance: Move/move-and-attack spending at most half budget may finish at any heading; spending more permits one-side rotation. Increased dodge permits any final heading. The summary free-turn wording does not override committed attack prohibition.
entries.implementation_note: Pure movement-value and heading assessments authored; persistent path execution, budget reconciliation and integration remain pending. Fixtures unrun.

entries.acceptance: A step permits its normal hex distance in any direction and free facing before/after. Terrain/posture movement point costs do not reduce step distance; still validate actual traversal, space and specific maneuver restrictions.

Eligible movement maneuvers allow at least one hex despite high costs. This is not permission to enter solid terrain, ignore sitting prohibition, bypass enemies or traverse impossible obstacles; document exact precedence.
A declared wait can interrupt a path between hex entries. An actor who has not moved can take the allowed step and strike; a surviving mover resumes with remaining budget and updated state.

Close reach targets own hex; forward reach one/two/three uses the depicted three/five/seven-cell front rings. Keep current weapon grip separate from maximum weapon reach and reconcile increased body-size reach under B402.

Reach at least two can attack through an ally without penalty or an enemy at -4. A line on a hex boundary is obstructed only if both adjacent cells are occupied, treated friendly unless both occupants are foes.

Side, rear or unseen melee attacks use the worse of -5 or visibility penalty and cap final skill at nine. No selected hit location; randomize if locations enabled. Wild thrust reach cannot exceed one yard.
Wild committed attacks cannot select the accurate +4 option. Combining wild with move-and-attack uses the more severe penalties rather than adding duplicate penalties.

Peripheral vision permits ordinary two-handed side attacks and same-side one-handed attacks; opposite-side and rear attacks remain wild. All-around vision removes wild classification but imposes -2 for rear/opposite-side awkward attacks. Specific techniques can override independently.
Ranged eligibility follows the diagram’s ordinary, peripheral or all-around vision arc. Exact boundary hexes require diagram-based coordinate fixtures before implementation completeness.

Shooting outside vision arc or without sight uses -10 and final skill cap nine, forbids aim and inherits random-location restrictions. Preserve stray-shot consequences rather than treating a miss as harmless.

Select a straight line between some part of shooter and target hexes that avoids solid obstacles. Each intervening person imposes -4; a shared edge imposes one -4 only if both neighboring hexes are occupied. Record chosen line to reuse for misses.

Prone interveners do not obstruct unless shooter is grounded; kneeling/sitting interveners do not obstruct unless shooter or target is likewise low. Wrong-target text uses a shorter same-level rule; reconcile exact posture combinations explicitly.
Intervener size at least two above shooter completely blocks sight, or three if kneeling/horizontal, four if prone, unless elevation permits seeing over. This is denial, not another -4.

On ranged miss check possible targets along actual shot line nearest first at min(9,intentional target score). Boundary-pair ordering is random. Miss/dodge continues; hit or successful block/parry stops. Use each target’s legal defenses.
After intended target dodges, continue stray checks only beyond that target. Successful block/parry ends the projectile path. Do not reroll for nearer bystanders already passed.

Opportunity fire requires stationary wait, facing a declared watched area entirely inside vision arc and doing nothing else. Keep opposing players’ declarations private. Trigger first entrant unless discrimination was selected.

Several opportunity attacks on the same entrant resolve simultaneously. Snapshot eligibility before consequences and avoid sequentially suppressing an already-triggered attack merely because another hit resolves first.
Ordinary opportunity fire gets no aim bonus. Watching exactly one hex is an exception: each waiting second also accumulates aim; apply the actual accumulated duration when triggered.
Covering one straight crossing line applies -2 instead of watched-area band penalties.

Optional target discrimination uses a hidden vision check when a target appears and adds -2 attack penalty. Report perceived friend/foe, not omniscient identity; author the failed-perception result contract.

Eligible thrown, firearm or crossbow attacks can emerge no more than one hex, shoot and return to cover in one attack maneuver. Bows/slings are excluded; no aim, -2 attack. Trigger opportunity attacks while exposed and permit only dodge against them.

Side attacks give -2 defense unless vision capability removes it. Shield block still cannot cover weapon side; one-handed parry cannot cover opposite side unless arm flexibility or body flexibility permits.

Rear attacks prohibit defense without suitable vision: peripheral allows -2, all-around none. Rear parry adds another -2 and rear block is prohibited unless stated flexibility exceptions apply; define exception precedence precisely.
An attacker observed starting in front then running behind is treated as a side attack for defense, not an unseen rear attack. Track origin and awareness during the path.
Retreat moves a step directly away, cannot enter occupied hex and permits one-side facing change. Close-combat retreat uses its own three-hex exit rule.

Any sufficient movement can enter a foe’s hex, immediately starting close combat. Move/move-and-attack/committed attack may stop there facing foe; continuing through requires evasion or collision within maneuver permissions.
Store entry side within a shared hex. Entrant occupies the near half and foe the far half; crossing into far-side front hexes requires evasion. Hex coordinate alone is insufficient.
Evasion requires enough movement to both enter and leave the enemy hex. Ending movement within it cannot count as successful evasion.

An unrestrained actor can leave through the three near-side hexes, paying direction/turning costs on movement maneuvers or using a step. Passing to far side requires evasion; grappling restricts departure under its detailed exceptions.
Melee attacks require close reach; ranged attacks use bulk instead of ordinary speed/range penalty. Other accuracy and legality requirements remain applicable.

Readying in close combat requires dexterity; failure consumes the action without progress. Fast draw needs both dexterity and skill checks; failed fast draw but successful dexterity uses a full ready action. Grappled-ready failure drops the item instead, requiring explicit precedence.
Close combat permits ordinary dodge, and parry only with free hand or close-reach weapon; block is forbidden. Unrestrained retreat exits through a legal near-side hex and grants normal bonus.

Shield retains applicable defense bonus but penalizes attacks by its bonus after the initial entering attack, and dexterity checks after the first close-combat turn. Removing it costs one ready turn and successful dexterity check.
Multiple participants can share close combat; record actual shared occupancy even if visual display places markers nearby. Do not infer mechanical separation from display layout.

At most two attackers combine takedown or three combine pin. Use strongest relevant score plus floor(each helper’s relevant score/5); retain each participant’s actual contribution, availability and restraint state.

Attacking into others’ close combat adds -2 plus posture modifiers. Target uses close defenses. Miss or dodge checks other occupants at min(9,intentional score), randomly ordering candidates, until exhausted or a hit; reconcile successful parry stopping with ranged stray rules.

Head/front controls multi-hex movement distance, heading and vision; body follows and can sweep farther than head. Persist full footprint path and authored body geometry, including potential collisions from swept portions.
Multi-hex actor cannot pass a gap narrower than its widest part; partial wall hex leniency needs explicit authored map clearance. Head-only path validity does not prove whole-body legality.
Multi-hex front/side/back regions follow the illustrated body outline, while sight originates at head. Rear body can lie outside own vision. Define coordinate fixtures for each supported footprint.

A figure occupying at least two hexes moving through a smaller figure resolves a collision giving the smaller actor defense. Larger actor continues unless itself knocked down; retain remaining path and movement budget.
Crouching adds one half point per hex.
Kneeling adds two points per hex.
Crawling adds two points per hex.
Lying spends the entire allowance to move one hex.
Sitting prohibits displacement.
Each minor obstruction, including ally or grounded body, adds one point.
Severe obstruction requires bypass or legal jump, not an invented finite surcharge.
Enemy occupancy requires the applicable close-entry/evasion procedure.
Poor footing adds one point or an explicitly authored greater cost.
Stairs in either vertical direction add one point per hex.
Water depth at most one sixth actor height adds one point per hex.
Deeper water consumes all movement points for one hex; reconcile swimming modes separately.
Watching 1 through 1 hexes gives attack modifier 0. Validate area size and entire arc before reserving opportunity fire.
Watching 2 through 2 hexes gives attack modifier -1. Validate area size and entire arc before reserving opportunity fire.
Watching 3 through 4 hexes gives attack modifier -2. Validate area size and entire arc before reserving opportunity fire.
Watching 5 through 6 hexes gives attack modifier -3. Validate area size and entire arc before reserving opportunity fire.
Watching 7 through 10 hexes gives attack modifier -4. Validate area size and entire arc before reserving opportunity fire.
Watching 11 through unbounded hexes gives attack modifier -5. Validate area size and entire arc before reserving opportunity fire.

exclusions.reason: Miniature-product promotion, source artwork and illustrative prose are excluded; diagram-derived geometric requirements are retained without reproducing artwork.
